subject: english
question:
Select the word segment that can substitute and replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence.

The toddler asked for more pieces of cake, but she wasn't given (more cake).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "any" is used correctly in the sentence to indicate the absence of additional cake being given to the toddler.
 
• The word "many" would not fit correctly, as it is typically used for plural countable nouns, and "cake" is uncountable in this context.
 
• "None" would imply that the toddler was not given any cake at all, which contradicts the context as the toddler had already received some cake.
 
• "Two" would not make sense in this context, as the sentence does not specify the toddler asking for a specific quantity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The toddler asked for more pieces of cake, but she wasn’t given **any**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​****Option 2: "many"** – Incorrect, as "cake" is uncountable in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "none"** – Incorrect, as it implies no cake was given at all.
 
• **Option 4: "two"** – Incorrect, as there is no reference to the toddler asking for a specific quantity.
